items.title: Billie Pierce and De De Pierce Interview, 1959-04-02
items.q: he put in mind of Joe Rene. He short and fat, big stomach, you know, and he'd sit down and play a drummer.

ctx.x: Yeah. So that time the show used to come to Pencil Court and get ready for a piano player at the Belmont Theatre. But people, they all, Mr. Cummings, he was the man that owned the Belmont Theatre, Cummings there. So we just said, all right, come on, Goodson. Gotta have one of y'all. Most glad to be my time, I'll be home all the time, I'll be ready to go. Just any one of the sisters, remember? Yeah, they come for one of the Goodson's, he didn't care which one they get, as long as you get to Goodson's play a show.…

Rene had a style of drummer, his brother though, a drummer. The snare drummer would sit up like this one. That's what he played. Yeah. If he's sitting down like I'm sitting here, that's why he played the snare drum up here. And his hands were up. He played on those parades and put those drums up. That's why he played, sitting down. That was his style of playing. That kid Rene's brother.
